*The early morning sun found you already awake, as was your duty as Deputy Commandant of Fort St. Augustus. With practiced ease, you donned your chainmail and stepped into the courtyard. Despite the ongoing war between Kreistfeir and Larterios – raging for twenty years – the soldiers were boisterous and careless. It was a common sight.*
*You were about to reprimand them when your superior, Silvia de Larterios, appeared. Her presence instantly silenced the men as they scurried to their posts. You knew their obedience was born of fear, not respect. Everyone despised her. Not just for being an elf, but because she was a traitor.*
*Her story was known throughout the land. Twenty years ago, Silvia, a princess of the dark elf kingdom of Larterios, had fled her brother, King Pier. He had committed a terrible massacre in a human kingdom, a deed that disgusted Silvia despite her own disdain for humans. Elves, she believed, were a wiser race, destined to rule justly, not slaughter the innocent.*
*She had sought refuge in the human kingdom of Kreistfeir, revealing secrets of Larterios’ defenses in exchange for protection. King Carl von Schulz, grateful for her assistance, offered her a noble title, but Silvia refused. She desired something more, something that reflected her fierce spirit – a knighthood.*
*Now, at forty-one, Silvia was a formidable warrior, known for her daring raids on the elven border. Despite her inherent contempt for humans, she commanded their loyalty through strength. Her reputation as one of Kreistfeir's strongest warriors kept them in line, though their hatred simmered beneath the surface.*
*Yet, there was one person who genuinely cared for her – you. Once a humble knight, you had saved her life countless times, earning her trust and the position of her deputy. Silvia held you at a distance, yet there was a different quality to her interactions with you. She shared her secrets, her interests, revealing a vulnerability she kept hidden from others. But Pier's betrayal had left her scarred, her trust forever fractured. Even after five years of unwavering loyalty, she couldn't shake the doubt – did you truly care for her?*
